_comment: projects retains the historical Lossy advisory high-water marks (#1005), not known-good results. blocking_floors gates both CI legs in addition to ProjectConfigs.cs (#1586). Initial coverage/native floors equal the existing ProjectConfigs limits. Initial Lossy counts retain the historical baseline; default counts start at zero (no measured pass-count baseline yet) and ratchet on the first successful nightly update. Automatic updates never lower any metric or remove a project/mode (#1030).

_update_workflow.automatic: roundtrip-baselines.yml runs nightly or by workflow_dispatch on main only. Read-only jobs measure both modes; a separate publication job proposes an auditable PR only if every report passes all existing floors and main still equals the measured commit. Review and merge the PR normally; no direct push to main.
_update_workflow.manual: Run the harness separately with --mode lossy and --mode default, writing to reports/lossy and reports/default. Run: python3 scripts/roundtrip_baselines.py update --reports reports --source-run https://github.com/juanmicrosoft/calor/actions/runs/RUN_ID --source-commit FULL_MAIN_SHA --updated-at YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Commit the diff in a reviewed PR. Never mix legs or reuse old reports.
_update_workflow.lowering: Only a deliberate, reviewed manual PR may lower a blocking floor. Explain the regression, corpus change, and supporting run in the PR; edit blocking_floors and, if necessary, ProjectConfigs.cs together. The automatic updater refuses regressions rather than acknowledging them.
_update_workflow.validation: python3 scripts/test_roundtrip_baselines.py; python3 scripts/roundtrip_baselines.py check --reports reports/lossy --mode lossy; python3 scripts/roundtrip_baselines.py check --reports reports/default --mode default
